title: A robustness pass over the V1 known gaps: the laser's leftovers, Isao's crate and his animated gate repair, the MK-9's ignition and its one release a pass, the seat's first-use hitch halved, and SOL-82 burning every building
context: docs/STATE.md listed eleven known gaps from the 2026-09-16 playtest rounds. Eight of them were taken in one pass on a worktree branch off main e3e345ab. The last and largest — no second gate, so the back door stays open once it is cracked — was deliberately not started: making plan.gate a list touches the story base's single gate mixer and open/close rule, base-print's gate plot, the pathfinder's gate rule in src/td-tab.js under its 13,505-line budget, the sector loop's gate integrity and pressure, Isao's repair orders and the HUD's GATE line, and a half-converted plan would have put the seven finished items at risk. Two of the eight (the gunship seat's hitch) had been started by an earlier agent and cut off mid-measurement; that work was re-read rather than trusted.
outcome: Seven gaps closed and one halved. SOL-82's scorch, smoke and books clear on NEW RUN and a page that asked for the laser keeps it through sector 1. Isao flies to the dropped crate and beams it before the part counts as received. The MK-9's ignition is its own burst at 3 m rather than the 25 mm impact pop that swallowed the seat and the feed, and one release a pass is proven end to end in the browser. The gunship seat's first-use hitch was measured honestly and halved: the cost was never the optic's own materials but the base's, linked a second time because the game's frame goes through the bloom chain into a render target (srgb-linear) while the spotting monitor draws the same scene straight to the canvas (srgb), and the output colour space is part of a program's cache key; src/fx/program-warm.js pays that bill a few objects a frame while the game runs, deduplicated down to the signature a program is actually keyed on. SOL-82 now burns every building, not only the Stalheart, and a burned one costs the colony its build step's perk for the rest of the run. Isao's gate repair is a print you can watch, his beam laid on the door's own footprint with GATE % climbing under it. The second gate is not started and is documented as still open.
alternatives: The cut-off WIP's fix for the seat hitch warmed the gunship optic's own rings, tracers and hull through a new `warm` parameter on createGunshipOptic. Dropped: the measurement it came with shows the eighteen programs linked at the seat were BASE_KIT_GAME, Skirt/carbon, Slab/concrete, Lift field/cyan, SH02_SALVAGE, AFR_VERTEX_PALETTE and BackgroundCubeMaterial — the base's, never the optic's. Its measurement harness was kept and is what made the real cause visible.

Warming the programs with one renderer.compile over the whole scene at load. Rejected: structures print all run long under Isao's build programme, so a single warm at load goes stale, and one compile of everything is the same 60 ms bill paid in one piece.

Warming against one render target only. Measured both ways round and rejected: binding the canvas alone leaves the chain's programs to link at the seat and binding a target alone leaves the canvas's, so the hitch simply moves. Both bindings are warmed.

Re-queueing a burned building on the build programme so Isao prints it back. Rejected as the safer and more honest reading of 'misuse can lose buildings': the step stays done and the colony goes without for the run.

Testing Isao's animated gate repair in --sectors. It cannot work there: storyApi.build() returns early on !story.grow, so a static stage=6 base never takes a repair at all. The step lives at the end of --grow, where the base really grows.
Starting the second gate anyway and leaving it partly done. Rejected under the instruction to leave a clear note rather than force it.
evidence: npm test (120 test programs) and npm run check green on every commit; src/td-tab.js held at its 13,505-line budget throughout (net zero in four commits).

The seat's hitch, --gunship, a 2.5 s watch on the call against 2.5 s of baseline just before. Before: one 64 ms long task, longest frame 78.6 ms against an 18.5 ms baseline, 18 shader programs linked (31 -> 49). After: no long task on the call, longest frame 65.9 ms against an 18.8 ms baseline, 9 programs (46 -> 55); the second seat is 18.5 ms and links none. The warm walk drains before the seat: 185 kinds, 366 compiles, nothing queued.

The nine programs that still link at the seat were not explained. Their cache keys differ from the warmed ones by the output colour space field, which src/fx/program-warm.js already binds both ways; the residual difference may be a light-count field the diff could not tell apart. The module says so in its own header. Narrowed and measured, not closed.

SOL-82 burning a building, --laser-game on a stage-6 base: the scope reads OURS UNDER THE BEAM · SOLAR over the solar complex (artifacts/browser/laser-game-building-warned.png), and after the burn the pad is bare and burning under a SOLAR LOST · station offline toast (artifacts/browser/laser-game-building-lost.png), with perks [gate, stalheart, station, gunship] -> [gate, stalheart, gunship] and lost [solar]. NEW RUN still clears the books.

The pure rule for a lost building is in test/build-programme.mjs: the radar takes the uplink, HUGIN the gunship bonus, the bays the spare hulls, the assembly line the rebuild; a building that never stood cannot be burned; one no step printed (the AFR-01 foundry) is still lost but has no perk to take; a perk another standing step still pays for stays on.

Isao's animated gate repair, --grow: the repair order carries a print bed, and the gate climbs 22.1 -> 60 hp in at least four distinct steps and never backwards over nine seconds of sampling. artifacts/browser/grow-gate-repair.png shows the HUD reading GATE DOWN 36% beside ISAO > printing GATE 16% +1.
Reproduce through the lock only: /Users/minikai/Dev/stalheart/scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --gunship | --laser-game | --defense | --grow.
Not verified: the gate-repair screenshot is taken from the orbit view, so it evidences the two HUD numbers moving together rather than a ground-camera frame of the beam on the door itself.
